description:
📝 Notes
Jan 23, 2026
R&D daily sprint
Invited Amir Houieh Unbody io Noémi Biró Gabor Kerekes
Attachments R&D daily sprint 
Meeting records Transcript 
Summary
Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh discussed that the current app lacks a "signature experience," suggesting a "partner mode" or proactive behavior from Cibil as unique features, while agreeing on the necessity of clinician input for feature prioritization. They also defined the process for determining the app's signatures, combining user demand and market gaps, and reviewed operational updates, including the Carefinder launch, the compensation for vetting a forward deployed engineer, and a plan for handling old project tickets by relying on commit messages and templates for decision documentation. Gabor Kerekes, Amir Houieh, and Noémi Biró worked on the Cibil manifesto, debating the core values of AI as an amplifier that incorporates friction and avoids becoming a "comfort machine," with Gabor Kerekes emphasizing "integration over fragmentation" and Amir Houieh focusing on software as a utility and "living creature."
Details
Signature Experience and Essential Features Gabor Kerekes expressed that the current app features lack a signature experience, suggesting that a "partner mode," which focuses on the social aspect of AI as a facilitator of relationships and extends app use to multiple people, could be a new and unique idea. Amir Houieh agreed that while current features are essential, they may not be "signature," though wellbeing activities could be uniquely designed or enhanced by a strong memory layer (00:24:49).
Manifesto and Prioritization of Features Gabor Kerekes suggested that Cibil needs a manifesto or ground values to make a statement about its purpose, such as facilitating relationships between a person and themself, or between humans and AI (00:25:53). They raised the question of whether the product should prioritize relationships with others for healing, suggesting that this would require a decision on whether to prioritize that aspect over standard features. Both agreed that increased communication and information exchange between different parties within the project is crucial (00:27:29).
Clinician Input for Feature Prioritization Gabor Kerekes emphasized the necessity of incorporating dialogue with clinicians into the feature prioritization process, as their expertise can provide valuable input on what effectively helps people. They stressed the importance of not assuming guided modules are essential and being more sophisticated in forming assumptions and hypotheses by consulting clinicians (00:28:39). Noémi Biró agreed, suggesting that claiming close collaboration with clinicians would be a significant trust builder, provided it is genuine (00:35:02).
Proactive Behavior as a Signature Feature Amir Houieh suggested that proactive behavior from Cibil, such as checking on users or recalling past conversations and articles, is missing and could be a signature or essential feature. Gabor Kerekes agreed that proactive behavior, such as asking a user about a past session or actively reaching back into memory during a conversation, would differentiate the app from standard tools like ChatGPT (00:32:00). Amir Houieh proposed bringing the proactive behavior idea under the "signature" category (00:35:02).
Process for Defining Signatures and Future Development Amir Houieh outlined that defining the app's signatures should involve addressing two questions: what users demand, and what Cibil can offer or what is missing in the current market, including the clinician's perspective (00:35:02). Noémi Biró confirmed that they are working on translating the feature ideas into a "how" for a collaboration process with clinicians. Amir Houieh also noted that the "local first small language model" is fascinating but may be too early for next week's focus, suggesting it be treated as a discovery item (00:36:17).
Hiring and Compensation for Forward Deployed Engineer Amir Houieh provided an update on the operational agreement regarding a forward deployed engineer, stating that if they are hired, there will be a mutual agreement on whether to move them to Cibil, and if so, the team will be compensated for vetting them. They also clarified that a six-month duration mentioned previously would be removed from the agreement (00:37:16).
Carefinder Launch and Functionality Amir Houieh announced the launch of Carefinder, an application that took one and a half years to develop, and showcased its features, including finding profiles based on user input, aggregating information generated from knowledge bases, and checking insurance coverage (00:38:41). They demonstrated how users can interact with the system using human language to find specific therapists, and that the next step is connecting the therapists' calendars for direct booking (00:41:28). The onboarding process for therapists is currently manual but will eventually open up for self-creation of profiles (00:43:10).
Management of Project Tickets and Documentation Noémi Biró mentioned reorganizing Notion and R\&D, noting an issue with a backlog of old technical tasks in Linear (00:43:10). Noémi Biró and Gabor Kerekes discussed the time spent assessing ticket relevance, leading to a decision to wipe old tickets at the end of a cycle and recreate them if they become relevant (00:44:31). Noémi Biró raised concerns about the potential loss of valuable context and decision documentation when wiping tickets, especially for future teams taking over the codebase (00:46:34).
Documenting Decisions via Commit Messages Amir Houieh suggested relying on comments and commit messages to document decisions, risks, and future considerations related to code implementation (00:48:27). Gabor Kerekes agreed and suggested creating a commit template to ensure important context, like alternative solutions considered, is captured in the commit history, which can be easily accessed by tools like Claude (00:49:32). Noémi Biró included this approach in the organizational operational agreement (00:50:37).
Meeting Schedule and Bug Fixes Noémi Biró confirmed a meeting with Melissa and Amir Houieh on Monday to kick off the next four weeks, gain clarity, and establish timelines for working with clinicians. Gabor Kerekes updated that they would push and deploy a fix for new conversations today (00:50:37). Amir Houieh confirmed they need to fix one bug today. Gabor Kerekes and Amir Houieh discussed an animation glitch on iOS, which Amir Houieh suggested might be fixed by removing backdrop filters (00:52:15). They aimed to deploy a version with major bug fixes tonight, keeping the work within the estimated 16 hours for bug fixing (00:53:32).
Handling Analytics and Reporting Noémi Biró relayed a request from Melissa for the analytics (00:54:43). They discussed creating a more automated or structured process for sending the weekly analytics, with Gabor Kerekes mentioning a script they created to generate TSV files. Gabor Kerekes also mentioned conducting fast research on lightweight analytics tools that could be implemented in the future as part of the admin panel (01:10:50) (01:13:49).MANIFESTO DISCUSSION
Manifesto Discussion Preparation Gabor Kerekes and Noémi Biró agreed on a plan for the manifesto discussion where each person would present their main statements and points rather than reading their full draft. Gabor Kerekes confirmed they had written a sketch of the manifesto and needed to finalize some points (01:13:49).
Iterative Thinking and Manifesto Development Gabor Kerekes proposed using the iterative thinking prompt with Claude to generate questions and synthesize text based on the three individuals' threads of thinking. The goal is to identify commonalities and differences to facilitate a conceptual workshop, with the resulting synthesis contributing to a manifesto. Gabor Kerekes indicated that the existing manifesto drafts are located in the R\&D lab's conceptual tab (01:16:35).
AI Amplification and Collaboration Gabor Kerekes's initial manifesto draft centers on the idea of AI amplifying humans rather than replacing them. They articulated that AI should refine thinking and activity, fostering collaboration instead of replacement. They further explained that AI can manifest hidden patterns and unlock potential in humans, giving the example of using AI to rapidly realize a dreamt-up tool (01:18:17).
Integration Over Fragmentation Gabor Kerekes discussed the concept of "integration over fragmentation," which stems from their experience working on Cibil, where various interests like mental health, design, software engineering, and system building converge (01:20:32). They explained that Cibil provides a means to integrate these diverse parts of their personality and interests, although they noted a need to develop this concept further. Amir Houieh appreciated the structure of Gabor Kerekes's manifesto for covering different aspects—AI positioning, general mentality, and personal motivation—and its potential overlap with their own ideas (01:22:26).
Manifesto Structure and Inspiration Amir Houieh suggested that the final manifesto should cover multiple topics and different perspectives, addressing pillars such as their positioning on AI, workflows, and the type of product they are working on. Gabor Kerekes mentioned the "Thinking Machines" manifesto as an inspiration for making concise statements that articulate a core mission (01:25:26).
Friction and Personalization in Tool Design Gabor Kerekes emphasized designing tools that incorporate friction and are not built primarily for user engagement or traction, but rather to slow the user down and encourage reconnection with themself. The concept of personalization was defined as allowing the user's way of seeing and processing the world to shape the tool, rather than the user adapting to a tool designed for them (01:26:46). They gave an example of a system built with a memory of their mental state and goals that introduces friction by rejecting off-schedule requests to support their articulated life values and goals (01:30:17).
Software Agency and User Authority Amir Houieh raised the crucial question of defining the agency of the software, specifically how much power AI should have in decision-making, such as determining what is beneficial for the user (01:35:24) (01:39:54). Gabor Kerekes asserted that the ultimate authority remains with the user, and the tool should function as an accountability partner that helps enforce user-defined values and goals, without prescribing a specific lifestyle (01:38:21). Amir Houieh pointed out that the software's response to a user pushing back against its suggestions is a key example of defining the software's agency in the manifesto (01:41:22).
Autonomous AI and Value Alignment Gabor Kerekes described a form of software agency where the tool acts autonomously, such as conducting background research and synthesizing information, but always on the user's behalf and aligned with their defined interests. They clarified that the software should never make decisions about what is valuable to the user, but once the user defines their values, the software can help find more of that value, thus amplifying the user (01:42:55).
Addressing Destructive Behaviors and AI Safety The speakers discussed the challenge of software amplifying destructive or addictive behaviors if the user's intentions are not positive (01:44:19). Gabor Kerekes argued that the software should amplify the user's intentions to overcome addictive patterns (01:45:31). They connected this risk to the concept of AI safety, where uncritical validation can lead to "AI induced psychosis" (01:46:58). Gabor Kerekes emphasized the importance of intentionally creating friction in the design to prevent the tool from becoming a "comfort machine" (01:48:28).
The Psychedelic Analogy for AI Gabor Kerekes drew an analogy between AI and psychedelics, noting that both can manifest latent tendencies in the mind ("mind manifesting") and carry similar risks if used improperly (01:48:28). They suggested that AI tools with a therapeutic element, like Cibil, should potentially be integrated into a holistic approach with professional guidance, depending on the case (01:50:03).
The Future of Software as a Utility and Living Creature Amir Houieh presented their manifesto, focusing on making future software act more like a utility and a "living creature" that is less artificial. They referenced Gabor Kerekes's idea of a "ghost" system that is embedded everywhere and replicates the person (01:51:45). Amir Houieh also proposed that their team define themself as a lab or a collective to allow outsiders to join and align with their vision (01:53:04).
Rejection of the Software Container Idea Amir Houieh advocates for rejecting the concept of software being delivered in pre-fixed "containers" (apps or websites) decided by a central authority (01:53:04). They argued that the current model was a temporary placeholder and that AI now makes it possible to shift focus to the completion of the task, enabling a more intention-oriented experience, similar to how the human brain works (01:54:22) (01:58:04).
Emphasis on Building and Experimentation Amir Houieh stressed the importance of building, experimentation, and "learning by doing" over purely theoretical research (01:58:04). Gabor Kerekes agreed, stating that for them, research and building are the same, involving forming a hypothesis, building it, and testing it. They referenced the "Thinking Machines" lab, which also emphasizes immediately applying research to product design and vice versa (01:59:09).
Next Steps: AI Synthesis and Break Gabor Kerekes proposed ending the current conversation to obtain the transcript and feed it, along with the three manifesto drafts, into Claude for analysis. The participants agreed to take a 15-minute break while Gabor Kerekes set up the next step (01:59:09).
Suggested next steps
Gabor Kerekes will push and deploy the fix for the issue about new conversations being created today.
Amir Houieh will fix the bug related to links today.
Noémi Biró will translate the collaboration process with clinicians into the how.
Noémi Biró will send the cibil analytics file to Melissa after the manifesto meeting.
Gabor Kerekes will publish the script that generates TSV files to main and update the schedule to remind the group to send analytics every week.
Noémi Biró will reply to Melissa's email.
Amir Houieh will reformulate the information about the forward deployed engineer.
Gabor Kerekes will set up the next step with Claude using the transcript after the conversation ends.
